A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BPP-Search and StructuredOR work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A.1–A.7 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original modeling experiments and ablations in Tables 4–7, plus evaluations of the trained PRM and preference model in appendix Tables 17–18.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experiments, ablations, and reward-model evaluations in Tables 4–7 and 17–18. These retained outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation procedure, PRM training, pairwise preference scoring, BPP-Search, and Random Greedy algorithm remain unchanged. Figure 2's redesign preserves the same tree structure and does not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use StructuredOR, MAMO-ComplexLP, and NL4OPT for the same mathematical-modeling tasks. StructuredOR's 124 examples and domain coverage are unchanged; IndustryOR remains illustrative rather than an evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 4–7, including the CoT variants, SC, ToT variants, and PRM-guided search alternatives. The newly cited hierarchical reward-model work is not added to any experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain GPT-4o for the search comparisons, the same tree configurations, and the same accuracy and reasoning-step metrics. Tables 6–7 still evaluate the 30 StructuredOR, 72 MAMO-ComplexLP, and 143 NL4OPT problems identified as solvable by the policy model.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Table 7 retain the same comparisons of greedy variants, beam widths, and pairwise preference selection. The PRM scoring analysis and appendix dataset/modeling examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Experimental tables retain point estimates, and Table 1's descriptive dataset standard deviations are unchanged.

E6.justification: The benchmark, ablation, and reward-model result entries are unchanged in Tables 4–7 and 17–18. For example, Table 6 retains BPP-Search correct rates of 0.933, 0.722, and 0.804 for StructuredOR, MAMO-ComplexLP, and NL4OPT, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same search and scoring definitions, and Appendix A.6 retains the same computational-complexity expressions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: comprehensive StructuredOR modeling annotations and BPP-Search's claimed accuracy and search-efficiency advantages. Updated access information and citations do not change these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 softens the schema-compatibility limitation from 'many questions' being unparseable to 'some questions.' Section 5.2 also explicitly situates PRM-assisted ToT feasibility in operations research. These are limited qualifications; the mechanism explanations and Section 7 limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the tengwang0318/StructuredOR GitHub location with LLM4OR/StructuredOR and adds a Hugging Face dataset location. This changes documented access instructions; the PDFs do not establish changes to hosted contents. Implementation, data-format, and prompt details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Wang et al. (2025b), concerning hierarchical multi-step reward models, to the introduction and Section 2.2. The MLPrompt reference is updated from a preprint to its COLING publication, representing the same work. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Limited edits change Zehua Liu's affiliation, clarify 'mathematical model,' correct the Appendix A.2 heading to 'Operations Research Dataset Comparison,' and refine several sentences. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with smaller nodes, distinct colors for tree layers, and black directional arrows while retaining its topology and caption. Dataset links become footnotes, and nearby text reflows. Other figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 provides modest improvements in usability and presentation through the additional dataset access information and Figure 2's visual distinction between tree layers. The limited wording qualifications also clarify scope. Methods, empirical evidence, and detailed appendix documentation remain unchanged, so the overall gain is small.
